correctness.rationale: For R>8epsilon>0, the exact curvature radius R-8epsilon cos3theta is positive. At any common support direction a convex union requires coinciding unique support points, giving f=0 => f′=0 for f=epsilon cos3theta-z·n. Analytic anti-periodicity forces a sign-changing zero, necessarily of odd multiplicity >=3; solving f=f′=f″=0 gives exactly three possible z. At each candidate the identity cos3theta+3cos theta=4cos^3 theta gives only two cubic support switches and coincident support points, so the entire hull boundary belongs to the union. The candidate center is contained in both original and reflected bodies, proving radial coverage of the hull. Exact support integration gives perimeter 2pi R+32epsilon/3 and area pi R^2+32 R epsilon/3-4pi epsilon^2. The standard-library checker passed but finite cases are explicitly not a proof.

value.rationale: The minimum possible three centers in Schneider’s reflection-convexity problem is realized by a smooth, strictly positive-curvature, real-analytic constant-width family, unlike the explicit triangle and Reuleaux triangle examples highlighted by the 2016 foundational source. Beyond cardinality, all centers and the resulting symmetric union support, exact perimeter and exact area gain are obtained, with precise C2/non-C3 joining regularity. This is a natural exact classification of a geometrically motivated reflection property, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
